title: spec review: C-O7a v2: count the Planner's own usage from its transcripts into the pool, and `orchestrator pick <role>` (spec round 2 after T-0163; supersedes T-0118)
spec:
Why: the pool only counts tokens from worker JSON output (spawn.py run_claude usage), so the interactive Planner session, the largest consumer, is invisible; measured 2026-09-18: pool credited account A with 613k tokens while one Planner transcript summed to about 7.8M by the same metric (input + output + cache_read/10). Round 2 folds in spec review T-0163 (project-dir encoding, counter reset on rollover, tally inside pick, offset pruning); dispatched without a further spec review by Planner decision.

(1) pool.py: `encode_project_dir(path) -> str` reproduces Claude Code's projects/ directory naming: every character that is not [A-Za-z0-9] becomes '-' (so '/' and '.' both map to '-'; '/Users/k3ntaw/.claude-mem' → '-Users-k3ntaw--claude-mem'). Verify against a real directory name under one of the configured config_dirs and put that example in a test; if the real convention differs from this rule, follow the real one and say so in the summary. Pool.tally_planner(now=None): for each account, dir = <config_dir>/projects/<encode_project_dir(str(ROOT.resolve()))>; if it does not exist, print one stderr line per tick at most ("planner transcripts not found for <account> at <dir>") and continue; read *.jsonl there, only lines of type "assistant" with a timestamp in the current day and the current 5-hour window (window_started in pool_state); sum message.usage.input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens // 10 exactly as run_claude does; store per account planner_day_tokens and planner_window_tokens plus a per-file byte offset in pool_state so each tick reads only appended bytes (a shrunken file resets its offset; offsets for files that no longer exist are dropped). ROLLOVER: wherever Account.utilization() resets window_tokens/window_started or day_tokens/day, reset planner_window_tokens / planner_day_tokens to 0 in the same place (keep the offsets: incremental reading continues, only the counters restart); test that a rollover zeroes them and a later tally adds only new lines. Account.utilization and the daily-budget check include the planner numbers. Malformed lines are skipped, never fatal.
(2) daemon.tick(): call pool.tally_planner() at the start of each tick, wrapped like the stages (a failure prints one stderr line).
(3) status(): each account shows planner_day_tokens and the window utilization including them; `orchestrator status --plain` prints them too.
(4) cli.py: `pick <role>` (role in planner|scout|review|execute) FIRST calls pool.tally_planner() (so a standalone launcher gets fresh numbers even with no daemon running), then prints the id and config_dir of the account pool.pick(role) returns, or exits 3 with "hold: no account with headroom".
README.md: one paragraph "Planner usage is counted from transcripts" and the `pick planner` line under Run it.
Tests: tests/test_pool.py builds a fake config_dir with two JSONL files (assistant lines in and out of the window, a malformed line, a user line), asserts the sums, the offset resume on a second call, offset pruning for a deleted file, the rollover reset, the utilization change and the pick result flipping to B when A's planner usage crosses the cap, and encode_project_dir on a path with a dot; tests/test_cli.py covers pick output (and that tally_planner was called), and exit 3. No new dependency; finish with summary, files changed, failures-only test output; commit on the task branch when green.
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py: encode_project_dir_matches_claude_code, tally_sums_assistant_usage_in_window, tally_skips_malformed_and_user_lines, tally_resumes_from_offset, tally_prunes_missing_files, tally_resets_on_rollover, tally_raises_utilization_and_flips_pick; tests/test_cli.py: pick_tallies_then_prints_account_and_config_dir, pick_exits_3_when_none; all green
`orchestrator status --plain` shows planner_day_tokens per account after a tick in a test fixture; a missing transcripts dir prints one stderr line and never raises
No transcript content other than usage numbers and timestamps is read into memory beyond the current line, and nothing from transcripts is written to the bus or logs
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency; only the six scoped files change; committed on the task branch
